open_points.subject: OwnerFormField fields
open_points.question: Are the listed fields the definitive and exhaustive fields of OwnerFormField, or are they only proposals that may be changed or extended?
options: The three listed fields are final and exhaustive
The list is provisional and may gain or lose fields
The list is final after adding fields needed to identify the owning form and closed-list choices
open_points.default_guess: Treat the list as provisional and add the form identity and closed-list reference required by the model's stated meaning.

witness.initial: The release contains two owner forms and at least one field read as a closed-list choice.
events: A later model author treats the candidate list as exhaustive.
Another later model author adds a form reference and a choices reference.
outcomes: OwnerFormField contains only name, carrier and reads_as.
OwnerFormField also identifies its form and the permitted choice vocabulary.
witness.observer: The owner-interface and contract implementers see different model shapes.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField.name
open_points.question: Is name the machine field key submitted by the form, the human-visible label shown on the page, or a value required to serve as both?
options: Machine submission key
Human-visible page label
One canonical value used as both key and label
Separate key and label facts
open_points.default_guess: Make name the stable machine submission key and add a separate label fact if the interface needs display text.

witness.initial: An owner form displays “Project name” but submits the key project_name.
events: The release data provider creates the OwnerFormField row.
The owner interface renders and then reads the submitted form.
outcomes: name is stored as “Project name” and used as the visible label.
name is stored as “project_name” and used as the submitted field key.
witness.observer: The owner sees different labels, and the server reads different request keys.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField owning form
open_points.text: A row of the owner form table: one field of the owner's pages
open_points.question: Does a row belong to a particular page, form, or product action, and if so what fact identifies that owner; alternatively, must name be globally unique across every owner form?
options: Add the owning page/form/action as a fact
Require name to be globally unique across all owner forms
Treat equal tuples on different forms as the same reusable field definition
open_points.default_guess: Add an owning form or product-action reference as a fact; do not assume field names are globally unique.

witness.initial: The create-project form and correct-customer form both contain a field called name with the same carrier and reading kind.
events: The release provider records both form fields.
A consumer looks up the row for one of the forms.
outcomes: The two rows are the same value because all declared facts are equal.
The rows remain distinct because each names its owning form or action.
witness.observer: The owner interface may render or validate the wrong field definition.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormCarrier
open_points.question: What model kind and closed semantic alternatives does OwnerFormCarrier have, and precisely what does each alternative mean for where a field belongs?
options: A State 1 enum with exactly request and values alternatives
An existing model whose definition must be supplied here
A non-enum value model carrying additional ownership facts
open_points.default_guess: Define OwnerFormCarrier in State 1 as a closed enum distinguishing the request envelope from the owner's submitted values, with an explicit meaning for each member.

witness.initial: A field is present in an owner-interface submission.
events: One implementer classifies all submitted controls as values.
Another implementer classifies identifiers, revisions, or confirmations as belonging to the request itself.
outcomes: The field is carried in the values model.
The field is carried in the request model.
witness.observer: The contract and owner-interface implementations produce different request models.

open_points.subject: FormValueKind
open_points.question: What model kind and exact closed set of semantic reading categories does FormValueKind define?
options: A State 1 enum with text, whole-number, yes-or-no and closed-choice meanings
An existing model whose definition must be supplied here
A value model capable of carrying parameters for a reading kind
open_points.default_guess: Define FormValueKind in State 1 as a closed enum with the four semantic alternatives stated in the Meaning passage.

witness.initial: A release row has reads_as set to a value intended to mean a whole number.
events: One later author defines the type as a four-member enum.
Another later author combines whole numbers with general numeric input or adds further kinds.
outcomes: Only integral text is represented by this kind.
Decimal or other numeric text is represented by the same or an additional kind.
witness.observer: The owner-interface and model validators accept different facts for the same field.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField closed-list choices
open_points.text: as one of a closed list
open_points.question: For a field read as one of a closed list, where are the identity and permitted members of that list represented, and are they facts of OwnerFormField?
options: Store the permitted choices directly in OwnerFormField
Store a reference from OwnerFormField to a separately declared vocabulary or catalog
Derive the choices from name outside the model
FormValueKind itself denotes one universal closed list
open_points.default_guess: Add a typed reference to a separately declared vocabulary or catalog, because different form fields can have independently changing closed lists.

witness.initial: Two owner-form fields are both read as closed-list choices, one choosing person or company and another choosing active or archived.
events: The provider creates both rows with reads_as set to the closed-list kind.
The owner interface asks which choices to render and accept.
outcomes: The choices are recovered implicitly from each field's name or hard-coded by the interface.
Each row explicitly references its own declared vocabulary.
witness.observer: The owner sees different available choices, and submitted values are accepted differently.

open_points.subject: OwnerFormField product-action coverage
open_points.text: one field of the owner's pages — what the owner types or picks in a form
open_points.question: Which owner-interface pages and product actions read OwnerFormField rows, and does the table cover every mutable owner form or only a specified subset?
options: Every owner action implemented by a form reads this table
Only explicitly named actions read this table
Each page or action declares independently whether it uses the table
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit per-action or per-form declaration and cover every mutable owner form intended to be data-driven.

witness.initial: The owner interface contains create-project, correct-customer and confirmed erase forms.
events: One implementation uses OwnerFormField for every form.
Another uses it only for forms that collect ordinary business values and hard-codes confirmation forms.
outcomes: All three actions read release rows.
Only create and correction read them; erase confirmation does not.
witness.observer: The owner sees different release-driven form behavior, and later contracts disagree about which actions consume the model.
